Farms That Grow Up
In the future, more people will live in big cities. There may not be much space for farms nearby. So some people are building farms that grow up instead of out!
These are called vertical farms. Plants grow on shelves stacked high inside a building, like books in a bookcase. Special lights shine instead of the sun. Water drips onto the roots, and very little is wasted.
Vertical farms can grow lettuce and herbs all year, even in winter. The food is grown close to where people live, so it stays fresh.
One day, your salad might come from a skyscraper!

AnswerA: farms where cows and sheep live in cities
AnswerB: gardens that grow on the roofs of houses
AnswerC: shops in the city that sell fresh salad
AnswerD: farms where plants grow on tall shelves indoors

ComprehensionText:
The Rain Alarm
Every time it rained, Gran's washing got soaked on the line. Leo wanted to help.
He found a tin lid, a battery, two wires and an old bell. When raindrops filled the lid, the water would touch both wires and ring the bell.
The first test was a flop. The bell stayed silent, even when Leo poured a whole cup of water into the lid.
'Back to the drawing board,' Leo sighed. He moved the wires closer together and tried again.
That afternoon, dark clouds rolled in. Ding! Ding! Gran rushed out and grabbed her sheets just in time.
'Leo, you're a genius!' she laughed.
QuestionText: What did Leo use to catch the raindrops?
AnswerA: a cup
AnswerB: an old bell
AnswerC: a bucket
AnswerD: a tin lid

Be Bright, Be Seen
When the sun goes down, it is hard for drivers to see people walking or riding. That is why everyone should wear something bright at night.
First, light colours like white and yellow are much easier to spot in the dark than black or navy.
Second, reflective strips shine when car headlights hit them. They bounce the light straight back to the driver.
Last, a small light on your bike or bag shows people where you are, even from far away.
So before you head out at dusk, light up and stay safe!

AnswerC: A small light shows people where you are.
AnswerD: Drivers should drive slowly in the dark.

Every School Needs a Nurse
Every school should have its own nurse. Here is why.
First, children get sick or hurt at school all the time. A nurse knows exactly what to do with a bumped head, a bad cough or a nasty bee sting.
Second, teachers are busy teaching. When a nurse looks after a sick child, the teacher can keep helping the rest of the class.
Last, a nurse can teach us how to wash our hands and stay healthy, so fewer people get sick.
A school nurse keeps everyone safe and happy. Let's ask for one today!

Sugar Gliders
Sugar gliders are small possums that live in Australian forests.
A sugar glider has a thin flap of skin from its front legs to its back legs. When it leaps from a tree and spreads its legs, the flap opens like a kite. It can glide about 50 metres! Its long tail helps it steer.
Sugar gliders live in small groups. They sleep together in tree hollows during the day. At night, they come out to lick sweet sap and nectar from trees and to catch insects.
